method_one_line: Provides composable attention kernels over paged KV layouts, with separate specializations for prefill, decode and append phases.
gap_note: Optimizes attention per phase but keeps the KV dtype fixed and never allocates bits; no weight-side budget and no memory-constrained device study.

title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for On-Device LLM Compression and Acceleration
method_one_line: Scales salient weight channels by activation magnitude before 4-bit rounding and keeps activations in FP16, so W4A16 survives without mixed-precision storage.
gap_note: Weight-only W4A16 on-device: the KV cache is untouched and the per-channel scale search is not tied to a byte or bandwidth budget, so no split is available.

title: Characterizing Prefill and Decode Regimes for Edge LLM Inference
method_one_line: Separates and characterizes the prefill and decode regimes of LLM inference on edge hardware, reporting how each regime's cost behaves rather than assuming a single inference cost model.
gap_note: A characterization study: it does not quantize, so it yields no weight-vs-KV allocation rule, and the device set behind its regime split is not resolvable from the record...

title: ELLIE: Energy-Efficient LLM Inference at the Edge Via Prefill-Decode Splitting
method_one_line: Splits LLM inference into prefill and decode stages and schedules them across edge resources to cut energy rather than to maximize throughput.
gap_note: Splits work between phases but not bits between weights and KV: precision is held fixed, so the regime reversal is never tested at the bit-allocation level.

title: A Measurement Study of LLM Inference Trade-offs Across Edge Continuum Hardware
method_one_line: Benchmarks identical LLM workloads across cloud, edge-server and device-class hardware and reports latency, energy and quality trade-offs per tier.
gap_note: Cross-hardware measurement without an allocator: it compares existing precision configurations instead of choosing a weight-vs-KV split under a fixed budget.

title: Sometimes Painful but Certainly Promising: Feasibility and Trade-offs of Language Model Inference at the Edge
method_one_line: Empirically assesses whether language-model inference is feasible on edge platforms, quantifying latency, energy and quality trade-offs across model sizes and precisions.
gap_note: Feasibility framing with precision as a fixed configuration: no joint bit allocation and no prefill/decode-conditional objective.

title: Does Mixture-of-Experts Actually Help Inference on Consumer and Edge Hardware? An Empirical Study
method_one_line: Measures MoE versus dense inference on consumer and edge devices, isolating memory capacity and bandwidth effects from parameter-count effects.
gap_note: Architecture comparison at fixed precision: quantization bits are a control variable, not a decision variable, so no weight-vs-KV split is produced.

title: Seeing at the Edge: Energy Characterization of Vision-Language Model Inference on Edge Platforms
method_one_line: Profiles energy and latency of vision-language model inference stage by stage on edge platforms.
gap_note: Energy profiling for VLM pipelines; no quantization allocation, no KV budget and no LLM weight-vs-KV trade-off.

title: EdgeProfiler: A Fast Profiling Framework for Lightweight LLMs on Edge Using Analytical Model
method_one_line: Builds an analytical performance model that predicts edge latency of lightweight LLMs from memory and compute parameters instead of exhaustive measurement.
gap_note: Predicts latency but has no bit-width decision variable, so it cannot be used to search a weight-vs-KV allocation space.

title: Empowering large language models to edge intelligence: A survey of edge efficient LLMs and techniques
method_one_line: Surveys edge-efficient LLM techniques spanning compression, quantization, architecture adaptation and hardware co-design.
gap_note: Catalogues weight and KV quantization as separate families; the joint-budget question is absent from the survey's taxonomy, not just from its conclusions.

title: MELTing Point: Mobile Evaluation of Language Transformers
method_one_line: Measures end-to-end mobile inference of transformer language models, including energy, thermal behaviour and latency under realistic phone conditions.
gap_note: Phone-class measurement: quantization is a fixed deployment choice, so no allocation policy is derived and no 8GB laptop-GPU or Orin comparison exists.

title: PowerInfer: Fast Large Language Model Serving with a Consumer-grade GPU
method_one_line: Exploits activation locality to split hot and cold neurons between a consumer GPU and the CPU, so a large model runs on one desktop GPU.
gap_note: Solves placement, not precision: bit-widths are fixed and the KV cache is outside the budget, so it does not touch the weight-vs-KV split.

title: LLMCad: Fast and Scalable On-device Large Language Model Inference
method_one_line: Combines a small draft model with on-device speculative verification and memory-aware scheduling to accelerate on-device generation.
gap_note: System-level speedup with fixed precision; no quantization budget and no joint weight/KV allocation.

title: Energy-Efficient Small Language Model Inference for Mobile Agents via DVFS
method_one_line: Tunes dynamic voltage/frequency scaling for small-language-model inference on mobile agents so that energy falls under a latency constraint.
gap_note: Frequency-level energy control with fixed bit-widths: it cannot ask whether moving bits from weights to KV is the cheaper energy trade.

title: Offline AI Modules: Voice-First Offline Architecture, Hardware Reference Stack, and Quantization & Benchmarking
method_one_line: Describes an offline voice-assistant stack and benchmarks quantized LLMs across hardware tiers that include a Jetson Orin tier.
gap_note: Engineering report with per-tier benchmarks; precision is chosen per tier by hand and no joint weight-vs-KV allocation or regime-conditional rule is proposed.

title: Sustainable LLM Inference for Edge AI: Evaluating Quantized LLMs for Energy Efficiency, Output Accuracy, and Inference Latency
method_one_line: Evaluates quantized LLMs on edge hardware for energy efficiency, output accuracy and inference latency at several precisions.
gap_note: Compares off-the-shelf quantization levels on edge hardware; the bit budget is never split between weights and KV and prefill/decode are not separated in the objective.

title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
method_one_line: Generates synthetic long-context tasks with configurable length and complexity to measure effective context size beyond needle-in-a-haystack retrieval.
gap_note: A benchmark with no precision axis: quantization studies that use it confound context length with cache error accumulation instead of separating them.

title: ∞Bench: Extending Long Context Evaluation Beyond 100K Tokens
method_one_line: Extends long-context evaluation past 100K tokens with tasks requiring reasoning over the entire context rather than retrieval from it.
gap_note: Measures capability at one precision; no protocol reports the prefill-side and decode-side contributions to a quantized failure separately.

title: LongBench v2: Towards Deeper Understanding and Reasoning on Realistic Long-context Multitasks
method_one_line: Builds a long-context benchmark of realistic, reasoning-heavy multitasks with controlled input length and difficulty.
gap_note: Validity-focused benchmark with no precision variable; results are reported at one precision per model, so no KV/weight split can be read off it.

title: Outliers and Calibration Sets have Diminishing Effect on Quantization of Modern LLMs
method_one_line: Ablates calibration-set choice and outlier handling across modern LLMs and finds both matter far less than earlier quantization work assumed.
gap_note: Attacks the calibration axis of PTQ, not the allocation axis: no memory budget, no KV term, and no regime conditioning.

title: Coverage-Based Calibration for Post-Training Quantization via Weighted Set Cover over Outlier Channels
method_one_line: Selects calibration samples by weighted set cover so that outlier channels are covered under a bounded calibration budget.
gap_note: Improves calibration selection only; the quantizer's bit budget stays fixed and KV precision is untouched.

title: ReproEvalCard: A Reporting Standard for Reproducible Evaluation of LLM Pipelines
method_one_line: Proposes a reporting card that records the execution stack, data and evaluation protocol needed to reproduce an LLM pipeline result.
gap_note: A pipeline reporting standard with no field for bit allocation, memory cap, achieved bandwidth or phase-separated throughput — exactly the fields quantization needs.

title: An empirical study of LLaMA3 quantization: from LLMs to MLLMs
method_one_line: Evaluates ten PTQ and LoRA-finetuning methods on LLaMA3 from 1 to 8 bits, plus a LLaVA-Next-8B multimodal model at 2-4 bits, and reports non-negligible degradation in both linguistic and visual tasks at ultra-low bit-widths.
gap_note: An accuracy-only sweep at fixed bit-widths with no allocation policy, no KV precision control and no constrained-hardware measurement.

title: Are LLM Benchmarks Already Contaminated? A Systematic Review of Contamination Detection Methods
method_one_line: Systematically reviews contamination-detection methods for LLM benchmarks and assesses their validity.
gap_note: Explains why small benchmark deltas are unreliable, but never connects that to the size of the accuracy deltas that bit-allocation studies report.

title: Accuracy is Not All You Need
method_one_line: Shows that compression perturbs model behaviour such as safety and robustness even when task accuracy is preserved, and argues for behaviour-level evaluation.
gap_note: Behaviour-level evaluation without a systems axis: no latency/bandwidth objective and no KV-versus-weight allocation question.

title: Exploring the Trade-Offs: Quantization Methods, Task Difficulty, and Model Size in Large Language Models From Edge to Giant
method_one_line: Evaluates instruction-tuned models from 1B to 405B under four quantization methods across 13 datasets and finds that smaller models degrade sharply at 4-bit while 70B-scale models stay stable.
gap_note: Evaluation breadth without a systems axis: hardware is a fixed substrate and no allocation is optimized or even varied.

title: Identifying and Mitigating Systemic Measurement Bias in Production LLM Inference Benchmarks
method_one_line: Identifies systematic biases in production inference benchmarking (warm-up, caching, load mixing) and proposes controls for them.
gap_note: Serving-benchmark hygiene; it says nothing about quantization levels, memory caps or phase-separated measurement.

title: AutoTuneBench: Trustworthy Measurement for Agent Auto-Tuning of LLM Serving Engines
method_one_line: Defines a measurement protocol for auto-tuning LLM serving engines that separates run-to-run noise from real configuration gains.
gap_note: Engine-tuning measurement rather than precision allocation; no weight/KV bit decision and no edge device class.

title: Quantization Hurts Reasoning? An Empirical Study on Quantized Reasoning Models
method_one_line: Large-scale empirical study of quantized reasoning models showing drops that grow with reasoning depth and are hidden by aggregate benchmark averages.
gap_note: Documents degradation but proposes no allocation rule: it never asks whether moving bits from weights to KV would shrink the drop, and never measures 8GB hardware.

title: Quantization Meets Reasoning: Exploring and Mitigating Degradation of Low-Bit LLMs in Mathematical Reasoning
method_one_line: Aligns chain-of-thought steps to locate the first faulty step caused by PTQ, then restores it with a small curated supervised/preference fine-tune.
gap_note: Repairs reasoning damage by fine-tuning at a fixed low-bit weight setting: KV precision is untouched and the repair is not budget-aware.

title: RECAP: Calibrating Low-Bit Reasoning Models on the History They Read
method_one_line: Calibrates low-bit reasoning models on their own generated reasoning histories to reduce drift accumulated during long chains.
gap_note: Calibration-side repair for weight quantization; no KV bit budget and no regime-conditional allocation.

title: RATIO: Reasoning Analysis and Token-level Inference Optimization for Quantized Reasoning Models
method_one_line: Analyzes quantized reasoning traces and optimizes token-level inference so accuracy is recovered within a bounded generation budget.
gap_note: Optimizes tokens under a compute budget, not bits under a memory budget: no weight-vs-KV split is available.

title: AdaKVQ: Adaptive Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization For Efficient Reasoning Models
method_one_line: Adapts KV-cache precision per head and per token for reasoning models so long chains keep critical state at higher precision.
gap_note: KV-side adaptive precision for reasoning, but weights are fixed and the trade-off is never expressed against one 8GB budget or a prefill/decode objective.

title: LFQ: Logit-aware Final-block Quantization for Boosting the Generation Quality of Low-Bit Quantized LLMs
method_one_line: Quantizes only the final block with a logit-aware objective and leaves earlier blocks at higher precision.
gap_note: Places precision by output sensitivity without any byte or latency model, and does not allocate across KV at all.

title: ReQAT: Achieving Full-Precision Reasoning Accuracy with 4-bit Floating-Point Quantization-Aware Training
method_one_line: Uses 4-bit floating-point quantization-aware training to close the reasoning gap to full precision.
gap_note: Requires QAT and fixes one 4-bit FP format at training time; no KV allocation and no inference-time budget adaptation.

title: Balancing Compute in LLM Inference: Model Selection, Quantization, and Test-Time Scaling
method_one_line: Formulates a joint choice of model size, quantization level and test-time compute under a fixed compute budget.
gap_note: Optimizes a compute budget over model/quantization/test-time choices, not a memory-bit budget split between weights and KV, and does not separate prefill from decode.

title: Not All Bits Are Equal: Scale-Dependent Memory Optimization Strategies for Reasoning Models
method_one_line: Shows that memory-optimal precision placement for reasoning models depends on model scale and derives scale-dependent placement strategies.
gap_note: Closest budget-aware allocation work in this sub-area, but the budget is per-model memory without a prefill/decode term and without an 8GB edge measurement.

title: Quantization Inflates Reasoning: Token Inflation as a Hidden Cost of Low-Bit Reasoning Models
method_one_line: Shows low-bit models emit longer reasoning traces, so accuracy per token and end-to-end cost both degrade even when final accuracy holds.
gap_note: Identifies a cost-side effect of quantization but never allocates bits, and the inflationis not charged against a KV memory budget.

title: Integration of Chain-of-Thought and Program-of-Thought on 4-bit Quantized Small Language Models for Financial Question Answering
method_one_line: Combines chain-of-thought and program-of-thought prompting for 4-bit small language models on financial question answering.
gap_note: Prompting strategy at a fixed 4-bit setting: no allocation, no KV precision control and no edge-hardware measurement.

title: BitNet b1.58 2B4T Technical Report
method_one_line: Trains a 2B ternary-weight, 4-bit-activation model end to end and releases weights with integer-only inference kernels.
gap_note: Weights are 1.58-bit by construction, so there is no budget left to reallocate and no KV-cache precision policy is offered.
